title: Formspec Needs Document
description: A Formspec Needs Document per the Needs specification. An authored artifact recording why software should exist: plain-language Need records grounded in normative evidence (Rulespec assertion IRIs) or empirical evidence (Observation research records), with declared-absence fail-closed, an adoption lifecycle, and supersession-never-erasure. The Needs Document targets no Definition; downstream artifacts cite Needs via needRefs and need: generation anchors. Needs MUST NOT alter core behavioral semantics (required, relevant, readonly, calculate, validation).

x-lm.intent: Version pin for needs document compatibility

version.description: Version of this Needs Document. SemVer is RECOMMENDED.

url.description: Canonical URI identifier for this Needs Document. RECOMMENDED when external systems cite its Needs.

needs.description: Substantive payload. Each Need is an evidence-grounded plain-language statement of why software should exist, with lifecycle and revision.

statement.who: anyone submitting this application under a deadline
statement.want: a receipt I can save and show someone later
statement.why: if the agency loses my submission, I lose rights I actually had
statement.done: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when

x-lm.intent: The Need records; statement plain-language and grounding-or-declared-absence are the load-bearing rules

id.description: Stable identifier for this Journey. Unique within journeys[]. Referenced by need.journey.
Stable identifier for this Need. Unique within needs[]. Referenced by Experience needRefs[].id and by need:<id>@<revision> generation anchors. Renaming is supersession, not an edit.

x-lm.intent: The citation target for needRefs and need: anchors

journey.description: Grouping key. When journeys[] is declared, MUST resolve to a journeys[].id.

grounding.description: Evidence citations. Exactly one of grounding / ungroundedReason is present (spec S5.4); the oneOf below enforces it.

ungroundedReason.description: Declared absence of evidence. Closed enum: hypothesis (we intend to validate), team-consensus (held without a citable source), self-evident (evidence would be circular). Mutually exclusive with grounding.

x-lm.intent: Fail-closed declared-absence; silent ungroundedness is unrepresentable

origin.description: How this Need entered the document. Closed enum. Immutable for the record's life; adoption does not rewrite entry. ai-proposed requires proposedBy and files at status proposed.

x-lm.intent: Discriminates human-authored, AI-filed, and migrated needs; drives the adoption floor rules

proposedBy.description: REQUIRED when origin is ai-proposed. The filing actor.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Closed enum. proposed: candidate awaiting human judgment. adopted: a commitment (requires adoptedBy). superseded: replaced by a successor carrying supersedes (terminal). withdrawn: rejected or found wrong (terminal; the record remains).

x-lm.intent: Coverage partitions on adopted; superseded/withdrawn are history, never deleted

adoptedBy.description: REQUIRED when status is adopted; remains on once-adopted superseded/withdrawn records. MUST be kind human when origin is ai-proposed.

revision.description: Content revision covering statement + grounding (incl. ungroundedReason). Bumps on any content change; MUST NOT bump on status/adoptedBy/title/journey changes. Pinned by need:<id>@<revision> anchors.

x-lm.intent: The regeneration staleness base; anchors pin this value

supersedes.description: The need.id this record replaces. MUST resolve within this document to a record with status superseded.

Statement.description: The Who / What / Why / Done block. Plain language is normative (spec S4.1): readable by a non-technical reader, no spec vocabulary, no solution names. done MUST describe an outcome observable by the person in who.

who.description: The kind of person, as they would describe themselves. A population, not a system role.
examples: anyone submitting this application under a deadline

want.description: The need, stated the way that person would say it.
examples: a receipt I can save and show someone later

why.description: What happens if this is not met — the harm or the loss, concretely.
examples: if the agency loses my submission, I lose rights I actually had

done.description: The outcome the person in who would observe when the need is met. Not a system behavior.
examples: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when

examples.who: anyone submitting this application under a deadline
examples.want: a receipt I can save and show someone later
examples.why: if the agency loses my submission, I lose rights I actually had
examples.done: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when

x-lm.intent: Plain-language requirement statement; the verifiability bar lives on done

Grounding.description: Discriminated union on kind: assertion (normative channel — Rulespec IRI, cite never compile) or observation (empirical channel — product-local research record).

ref.description: IRI of the cited Rulespec assertion or artifact (e.g., urn:rkaf:workspace:<ws>/<localId>). Opaque to Formspec processors; Rulespec owns everything behind it.

x-lm.intent: The typed ref across the Formspec/Rulespec decision boundary

method.description: How the observation was made. Closed enum.

x-lm.intent: Empirical method; closed so coverage queries can partition by it

uri.description: Source of the observation (research repository entry, analytics query, ticket). Discovery-weight: not required to be content-addressable; promotion to a Rulespec assertion is the escalation.

observedAt.description: RFC 3339 date or date-time of the observation itself.

Excerpt.description: The quoted moment, Web Annotation TextQuoteSelector-shaped (oa:exact / oa:prefix / oa:suffix) so the quote is re-findable in its source.

examples: I screenshot every confirmation page because they lost my renewal once.

GroundingRole.description: Relationship of the evidence to the Need. motivates: shows the lack exists. constrains: bounds any satisfying solution. authorizes: establishes that meeting the need is permitted or mandated. constrains/authorizes shared with the References rel vocabulary.
